# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as ui from '../support/ui';

test.setTimeout(240_000);
test.describe("tree search", () => {
  test("tree search", { tag: '@functionality' }, async ({ browser }) => {
    const sheet = ui.sheetId();
    const pg_uma = await ui.userPage(browser, "uma", sheet);
    await ui.loadSheet(pg_uma, `${sheet}-p`);
    await ui.setToday(pg_uma, "2026-03-10");
    expect(await ui.setRate(pg_uma, {"grade": "A", "pct": "10.00"})).toBe(true);
    const p_pam = ui.must(await ui.addPerson(pg_uma, {"name": "Pam", "grade": "A"}));
    const p_bea = ui.must(await ui.addPerson(pg_uma, {"name": "Bea", "grade": "B"}));
    const c_pam_0 = ui.must(await ui.addClaim(pg_uma, p_pam, {"amount": "1.00"}));
    expect(await ui.claimAction(pg_uma, c_pam_0, "open")).toBe(true);
    await ui.loadSheet(pg_uma, sheet);
    await ui.setToday(pg_uma, "2026-03-10");
    expect(await ui.setRate(pg_uma, {"grade": "A", "pct": "20.00"})).toBe(true);
    await ui.setSetting(pg_uma, "parent", `${sheet}-p`);
    const p_ada = ui.must(await ui.addPerson(pg_uma, {"name": "Ada", "grade": "A"}));
    const p_ben = ui.must(await ui.addPerson(pg_uma, {"name": "Ben", "grade": "B"}));
    expect(await ui.addAlias(pg_uma, p_ben, "Pal")).toBe(true);
    const c_ada_0 = ui.must(await ui.addClaim(pg_uma, p_ada, {"amount": "10.00"}));
    expect(await ui.claimAction(pg_uma, c_ada_0, "open")).toBe(true);
    await ui.loadSheet(pg_uma, `${sheet}-c`);
    await ui.setToday(pg_uma, "2026-03-10");
    await ui.setSetting(pg_uma, "parent", `${sheet}`);
    const p_cal = ui.must(await ui.addPerson(pg_uma, {"name": "Cal", "grade": "A"}));
    await ui.loadSheet(pg_uma, sheet);
    expect(await ui.search(pg_uma, "a")).toEqual([`${sheet} Ada 2.00`, `${sheet} Ben n/a`, `${sheet}-c Cal 0.00`, `${sheet}-p Pam 1.00`, `${sheet}-p Bea n/a`]);

content.text:
The tree search is in place, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

There's a search box (`search-name`) and a Search button (`search`). Pressing it lists every person on this sheet and on the other sheets of its tree whose name or an alias contains the typed text, ignoring case. Each line (`search-line`) reads `<sheet id> <name> <due-total>`, and `search-count` shows how many lines there are. This sheet's people come first in list order, then the other sheets' people by sheet id. An empty search lists everyone.

**What I added:**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree`, returns the other sheets of the tree: the sheet's ancestors, then its descendants, counting only sheets that exist. It reuses the same tree definition the app already uses for name clashes.
- **Screen:** a new panel in `features/search/search.slot.tsx`. It reads each sheet's people and computes their due-totals the same way their rows on the people list do, so "n/a" appears where the person list shows it. It follows the same pattern as the existing consolidated header figures.

**Choices the request left open:**
- **Retired people are included,** even when "show retired" is off, because the request says "every person".
- **Searches show the sheets as they are now,** even if the screen is set to an earlier as-of date. The consolidated figures behave the same way. The tests never search under an as-of date, so this is untested.
- **Old results disappear on each press:** the count and lines are cleared, the tree and the other sheets' data are re-read, and the count only reappears once every sheet has loaded.
- **Sibling sheets are left out.** "Tree" means ancestors and descendants, not the whole tree from the top sheet down.

The search doesn't change any data, so it writes nothing to the audit file.
